Preliminary Study for Biometric based on Gait 
Pattern Analysis Using Insole-Type Force Sensor 
 
Hangsik Shin 
Department of Biomedical Engineering 
Chonnam National University 
Yeosu, South Korea 
hangsik.shin@jnu.ac.kr 
Hwa Young Jung and Se Dong Min 
Department of Medical IT Engineering 
Soonchunhyang University 
Asan, South Korea 
hwayung89@gmail.com and sedongmin@sch.ac.kr
 
 
Abstract—The purpose of this research is to investigate the 
significance of feature vectors for gait-based biometric 
technology. We developed the insole-type flexible textile force 
sensing module, and collected information of gait such as stride 
time, stance time, swing time, left-right ratio and amplitude from 
eight participants. Also, we evaluated the attribute of each 
feature using the chi-square test and the gain ration feature 
evaluator. The result shows that the significance is higher in 
order of following features; stride time (left), stance time (left), 
swing time (left), swing time (right), stride time (right) and stance 
time (right). However, significance was not found in amplitude of 
force signals and stepping phase. 
Keywords—Biometric, Festure Selection, Gait Analysis, insole-
type sensor, Pattern Classification 
I. INTRODUCTION 
Major topics of personal iden tification or biometric are an 
analysis of the physical or personal characteristic of each 
individual. Compared with th e traditional secure system like 
the personal identification number (PIN) or lock-and-key, 
individual’s physiological characteristic such as the face, 
fingerprint or iris has extremely high security. These features 
are very hard to duplicate, and it is free from the risk of loss as 
well as change [1, 2]. Moreover, biometric based recognition is 
useful to build a secure management system because it 
supports user tracking. The most important area of biometric 
focuses on the physical characteristic recognition. For example, 
fingerprint, palm print, iris, face, vein or hand shape is usually 
used as a unique individual features [2-5]. Among these 
techniques, fingerprint is widely adapted to the personal device 
like a smartphone. Some other biometric techniques are based 
on the behavioral characteristic. For example, gait pattern [6] 
and signature or voice also could be used for the personal 
identification. 
The biometric technology could be used in different ways 
according to its recognition method. A physical characteristic 
based technique like fingerprint recognition is suitable for the 
intended situation because it needs an accurate touch on the 
fingerprint sensor. Gait-based personal identification is an 
emerging biometric technology, and it has attracted interest 
because it is non-invasive and does not require the subject’s 
cooperation. In other words, gait pattern based recognition 
method could give an efficient sol ution for the unconstrained 
or unconsciousness identificati on. Gait-based identification 
technology is, however, still in developing stages. There are 
two representative gait-based identification techniques in 
development. First, video ba sed gait recognition has been 
widely used [7-9]. The second method uses a radar system to 
record various body parts movement during the gait cycle [10-
12]. However, no model has been developed that is sufficiently 
accurate and marketable. 
The purpose of this research is to investigate significant 
features of gait pattern as a preliminary study of gait-based 
personal identification. In th is research, we developed insole-
type gait recording system and extracted gait parameters of the 
recorded signal. Then, we calculated attribute rankings of gait 
parameters using statistical method to find significant features 
of gait-based identification. 
II. MATERIALS AND METHODS 
A. Insole-type gait pattern measurement system 
 To record gait patterns, we developed conductive textile 
based insole-type capacitive force sensor. Developed sensor is 
flexible and has a smooth surface, thus it is less irritating to the 
human body than rigid sensors. Fi g. 1 is a structure of the 
capacitive sensor which contains a shield layer between sensor 
plates. In Fig. 1, ̺a is a shield layer for adjusting the sensitivity 
between human body and sensor plate, ̺b is a layer where 
occur the capacitance changes, and ̺c is a shield layer to block 
an environmental noise and electromagnetic noise including 
the powerline interferences.
